report.subtitle: 30 games · compared with the other players in those same games

agenda:
Keep: late in a round your fights go better than players of your own level.

Work on: the early deaths where your view was elsewhere, and long-range fights taken with a weak gun.

Understand: you start your fights early. Re-check next time: how often you are the first player to die, and where your fights start on each map.

moments.title: You start your fights early, and take the first kill and first death more often
moments.question: How early do my fights happen, and what does it cost or win?

blocks.text:
More than a third of your fights start in the first twenty-five seconds of a round, against about three in ten for the players in your games. That fits the two numbers below: you get the first kill of the round more often than they do, and you are also the first player to die more often. Early fights are a swing in both directions.

The rounds that follow show two first kills and two first deaths, with where your view was pointing just before each one.

module.caption: Share of your fights that start in the first 25 seconds

blocks.text: The first kill of the round is worth having: your team gets the numbers until someone trades it back.

module.caption: Your kills that were the first kill of the round

picks.note: A clean opening. You are aimed at him for the whole second before, he dies to a headshot, and two teammates each get a kill within two seconds of yours. That is what a first kill is worth when the team is close enough to follow it up.

An even trade rather than a win. You and he are aimed at each other before it starts, you kill him, and he kills you two tenths of a second later. A first kill that costs you your life gives the team no numbers. Worth asking whether a flash, or a teammate on the same angle, could have made it a free kill.

blocks.text: You are also the first player to die a bit more often than the players in your games.

module.caption: Your deaths that were the first death of the round

picks.note: You are on Catwalk with the nearest teammate about eight hundred units away, and the T is close, about three hundred and sixty units. For the second before he kills you, your view is more than fifty degrees off him. Your team still won the round. Worth asking what you were looking at instead, and whether you knew he was that close.

The opposite case. You are aimed straight at him the whole time, so this is not about where you were looking. What stands out is the gun and the range: a P250 against an AK-47 from about eight hundred units. Worth asking whether this was a fight you had to take.

moments.takeaway: Early fights are your style. Take them when the team is close enough to trade and you are aimed at the angle; skip them when you are looking elsewhere or outgunned.

alternatives: Role: an entry or forward role produces more first kills and first deaths for anyone.
limitations: Both first-kill and first-death differences are exploratory: they are suggestive but do not survive the correction for running many checks.
The view angle is horizontal only, and looking toward a player does not mean they were visible.

moments.title: Late in the round you win your fights
moments.question: How do I do in fights after the first minute of a round?

blocks.text:
After the first minute you win more of your fights than players of your own level do in the same games. It is a small number of fights, so treat it as a lean rather than a certainty.

There are no replays here: the examples the software keeps for this finding are all lost fights, which would show the opposite of what the finding says.

module.caption: Fights won after 60 seconds, compared with players of your own level

moments.takeaway: Keep it. Late in a round, your fights go better; that is a reason to be patient when the early fight is not there.

alternatives: Late-round fights often come after trades have already thinned the round, so numbers may favour you.

moments.title: Where your fights start on Inferno and Nuke
moments.question: Where do I take my fights on each map?

blocks.text: As CT on Inferno, more than half of your fights start at Banana. For other players on that side the share is under one in five. That is a habit of position, not a result: it says where you spend your time.

module.caption: Inferno, CT: share of your fights that start at Banana

blocks.text: The same is true as T on Nuke, where about two in five of your fights start at Bombsite A, against about one in seven for the players in your games.

module.caption: Nuke, T: share of your fights that start at Bombsite A

moments.takeaway: You know your spots. Ask whether they are the ones your team needs, or only the ones you are used to.

alternatives: This is what a fixed role looks like in the data.
limitations: Few games on each map, so each is a small set of fights.
